QF.id: SIA Assessment Frameworks Techniques and Standards_40

question.text: Nari Shakti Trust ran a women-SHG program with investment of INR 25 lakh. Gross monetised outcomes: INR 90 lakh. Assumptions: deadweight 20%, attribution 25%, drop-off 10%, displacement nil. Compute the SROI ratio.

explanation.text: The Logic: Start: INR 90 lakh. After deadweight 20% → 72 lakh. After attribution 25% → 54 lakh. After drop-off 10% → 48.6 lakh. SROI = 48.6 / 25 = 1.944:1 ≈ 1.94:1. Positive (≥1:1) but modestly so — narrative should disclose assumption sensitivity. The Trap: 3.60:1 is gross (90/25). 2.88:1 applies only deadweight. 1.45:1 over-deducts. Correct application is multiplicative cascade in the order deadweight → attribution → drop-off. Cross-Exam Context: V-A Distributor and X-A IA use cascade discounting (fees → taxes → returns). XXIII applies analogous cascade to impact monetisation. Assessor's Pro-Tip: Present the cascade in a waterfall chart in the AIR: 90L → 72L → 54L → 48.6L, so a lay reader can see exactly where value leakage occurs and challenge any one deduction.
